newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-NEW ENGLAND WINS TWICE, SNAPS DALLAS WIN STREAK AT FIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW ENGLAND WINS TWICE, SNAPS DALLAS WIN STREAK AT FIVE.

text.p: The New England Revolution broke the Dallas Burn's five-game winning streak with a 3-1 victory Sunday to become the first Major League Soccer team to win consecutive home games the same weekend.

Second-half substitute Imad Baba scored goals in the 65th and 82nd minutes to lead the Revolution (8-4) into second place in the Eastern Conference. Mozambique National Team captain Chiquinho Conde also added a goal. Ted Eck had given Dallas (7-5) a 1-0 halftime lead.
On Friday, Argentine Alberto Naveda recorded the first hat-trick in team history to lead the Revolution to a 3-1 victory over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars.

After Venezuelan Giovanni Savarese gave the MetroStars (5-7) a 1-0 halftime advantage, Naveda took centerstage, scoring goals in the 57th, 71st and 90th minutes as the Revolution broke a scoring drought of 250 minutes at home.
D.C. United (9-3) remained in first place in the East with a pair of 3-2 victories on the road.

On Thursday, U.S. National Team captain John Harkes scored his first goal of the season and set up the game-winner by substitute John Maessner with nine minutes remaining to lead United to a 3-2 win over the Columbus Crew (6-6) in Columbus, Ohio.

Harkes equalised in the ninth minute after Jason Farrell had given the Crew the lead three minutes prior. Bolivian Jaime Moreno converted a penalty kick in the 17th minute, but Pete Marino tied it in the 75th minute.

On Sunday, United scored all of its goals in the second half of its 3-2 road triumph over the struggling San Jose Clash (4-8). United will lose its two Bolivian stars, Raul Diaz Arce and Moreno, for six games due to their commitments in Copa America this month.

Zimbabwean international Digital Takawira set up the tying goal and scored the go-ahead goal to lead the visiting Kansas City Wizards (6-4) to a 3-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy (3-8) and into first place past Dallas in the Western Conference.

After Bryan Taylor had given Los Angeles a 1-0 advantage, Takawira fed Paul Wright in the 71st minute and then scored in the 87th minute. Galaxy defender Greg Vanney scored an own goal in the 89th minute.
Los Angeles goalkeeper Jorge Campos, playing his first game of the season after completing his Mexican League commitments, was ejected in the 66th minute for a handball.
Mexican David Patino and former U.S. National Team captain Peter Vermes scored in the second half for the Colorado Rapids (5-7) in their 2-0 home triumph over the Tampa Bay Mutiny (5-6).

Marcus Hahnemann, the league's leading goalkeeper, recorded his third shutout as the Mutiny dropped below .500 for the first time in team history. Mutiny goalkeeper Scott Budnick was red carded for fouling a Rapids player on a breakaway in the 86th minute.
